findings.claim: A temp folder left after the mv (step 4 fails, for example on the folder-lock 409 already seen live on deletes, or a crash between steps 3 and 4) holds only .abstract.md and .overview.md. Catch-up never sees it, because files() drops summaries and folders (the errFolderLeft comment says so). Redelivery does not clean it either, because the retry picks a new random name. The plan's claim that catch-up's remove path deletes a leftover is true only for a crash before the mv. Without a fix, hidden summary folders, each describing an image, build up under the parent and stay indexed. The plan has to say how this case is cleaned: for example a temp name derived from the target URI, so the retry reuses and deletes it, or catch-up reaping .ovsync-upload- folders by name. It also has to say whether a failed step 4 fails the event, which would rerun the upload and the VLM call.

Catch-up can reap a live upload. A pass that walks the parent between add (step 2) and mv (step 3) sees <temp>/<name> as an unwanted file. It locks that temp URI, a different key from the uploader's file URI, and deletes it under tree.RLock, which runs alongside the uploader's RLock. The mv then gets 404 and the event retries the whole upload, VLM call included. The plan has to say how catch-up leaves an in-flight temp folder alone, for example by keying the temp folder to the target file's lock.

The plan sends every object that is not valid UTF-8 down the add-resource route, but the evidence covers only PNG. OpenViking's add resource parses formats (PDF, office documents, text in another encoding), so <temp>/<name> may not exist or may not hold the raw bytes. Then the mv 404s and the event retries 20 times, running a parse and VLM pass each time. The openviking-sync action is reusable by other repositories, so such files can arrive. Either limit the route to the formats proven (images) and say what happens to the rest, or spike: does add resource into a temp folder leave a PDF and a latin-1 .txt at <temp>/<name> with the same sha256?

Spike 3 always had the parent D already present (notes.md was written first). A binary whose folder does not exist yet in OpenViking is a real case: a folder that holds only images, or a PNG event that arrives before any text file in its folder on a first sync, since events come out of order. Does add resource with to=<missing D>/.ovsync-upload-x create the missing parents, the way content/write does? If it does not, those binaries never land. This is a spike question: add a PNG with to set two levels below a folder that does not exist, then mv and delete as in spike 3.
The temp folder is gone from the plan, so no leftover temp folder can build up.
No temp URI exists, so catch-up cannot reap an in-flight temp file.
The route is limited to image extensions, and every other non-UTF-8 object is skipped with an INFO line.
Spikes 4 and 5 show add resource creates missing parents without create_parent.

Catch-up and Apply decide 'image' by different rules, and catch-up's stale have snapshot then deletes the wrong URI. Catch-up picks D/name/name from the extension alone. Apply also needs the bytes to be invalid UTF-8 (r4). Case A, a .png key holding valid UTF-8 (a git LFS pointer is exactly this): Apply writes text at D/name. Catch-up wants D/name/name, sees D/name, calls Apply (rewrite plus summary cost), then removes D/name from the have snapshot it took before the write. The next pass finds nothing and writes it again. The file flips between present and deleted on every pass, forever. Case B, the migration the plan is for (r7): have = {D/name damaged plain file}, want = {D/name/name}. The first loop's Apply deletes the plain file and adds to=D/name, so D/name is now a folder holding the fresh image. The second loop then calls remove(D/name) with recursive=false on that folder, from the stale snapshot. Either it errors on every first pass after deploy, or it deletes the new image. Before this change a key's want and have URIs were the same string, so the two loops never touched one path. The plan has to give one rule that catch-up and Apply share. For example: catch-up counts D/name or D/name/name as present for an image-extension key, and never removes a have URI U when U/base(U) is wanted. Or Apply decides by extension alone and r4 changes. The plan should also say which URI the per-key lock uses, so Apply and catch-up's remove lock the same key for one image.

Deleting an image relies on the existing removeIfEmpty to drop D/name. D/name is a folder that add resource created as a resource root. In spikes 4 and 5, a folder created that way was still listed in its parent after a recursive DELETE that returned 200, three times out of three (estimated_deleted_count 2, then 0 on the retry). Spike 3 saw it go, so the result is mixed. removeIfEmpty checks the parent listing and fails with 'still listed after its delete' when the folder is still there. If spikes 4 and 5 show the normal case, every image delete returns errFolderLeft: events retry to MaxTries and go to dead-letter, catch-up cannot see the folder, and an empty D/name folder stays behind. r5 cannot pass against the real server. The plan does not list this risk. Spike question: on v0.4.17.1-9, after add resource with to=D/name (with D existing, and with D missing), DELETE D/name/name and then DELETE D/name recursive=true, wait=true. Is D/name gone from ls D right away, after a few seconds, or never? If it stays, what would remove it?

The ticket makes a design choice with a rejected alternative (store images in OpenViking's native per-resource layout D/name/name instead of at the exact URI D/name through a temp folder and fs/mv, which spikes 3-5 showed leaves hidden folders), but no decision record holds it. CLAUDE.md requires one per choice. The component page states the layout but not why the exact-URI route was rejected, or that the operator accepted that markdown image links now point at a folder.
